China’s renewable surge relegates coal to reserve role

China’s electricity system is progressively transitioning to one dominated by renewables, with coal-fired generation held in reserve to deal with periods of exceptionally high demand or when output from wind, solar or hydro is below normal.

Policymakers increasingly describe as coal as “ballast stone” and a “safety net” — backing up intermittent renewables in electricity generation and lessening the security risks of depending on imported oil and gas ...

Bessent is smart enough to know that you can’t kill oil prices unless you kill the backwardation in the curve. 

And you can’t kill backwardation unless you have the barrels. 

The US can announce another unilateral SPR release and let’s say that 70 million bbls is the minimum. 

That’s another 200 million bbls. 

But the release rate is throttled down to 0.5-0.6 million b/d. 

That’s not enough to kill backwardation. 

The barrels that were trapped in the Middle East have been released already, so there’s no more immediate supply he can use to dump on the market. 

Clock is ticking.

Strait of Hormuz over the last 24 hours: the 8th deal?

Since the TACO yesterday, Iranian news reported that the US may be willing to let Iran control inbound tanker flows. This is funny as shit because whoever controls inbound tankers essentially controls outbound flows. But who gives a shit about logic these days.

Just as the market was set to open on Sunday, the US sent a convoy through the Oman lane where a panamax, Velos Amber, was spotted with its AIS turned off right before it entered. You can see it in the video from @MarineTraffic.

Shortly after, UKMTO reported that Iran fired something at the tanker. It did not hit, but it was likely another warning signal.

What's clear is that the Oman lane is still active with firms like Kpler and other showing flows close to 3-5 million b/d.

What's unclear is when the Iranians will implement enforcement on the Oman lane, especially for inbound tankers.

I suspect we are near the end of this TACO nonsense. From an oil inventory standpoint, inbound VLCCs to the US will push commercial crude inventories to operational minimums just as SPR runs out at the end of August. Trump, along with the IEA, will have to announce another round of SPR.

It's now or never.
